title: Existence of the integral exceptional inverse image
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. Let $X,Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$, and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Regard $\mathcal O_E$ with its $\ell$-adic topology as a condensed coefficient ring, use the module-object pro-étale coefficient categories and bounded constructible subcategories $\Dbc$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and use the localizing closures of [sk-def-localizing-closure], with their ordinary ambient coproducts.

The functor
$$
Rf_!:\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))\longrightarrow\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E))
$$
of [det-prop-int-brown-construction], given at the chosen compactification $f=p\circ j$ by the restriction of $Rp_*D(j_!)$ with the module-object convention of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek], has an exact right adjoint
$$
f^!:\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E))\longrightarrow\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)),\qquad
\Hom(Rf_!M,N)\simeq\Hom(M,f^!N),
$$
naturally for every $M\in\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))$ and $N\in\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E))$. This adjoint is unique up to a unique natural isomorphism compatible with the counits (equivalently, with the adjunctions). Under the equalities $\Dctf(-,\mathcal O_E)=\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$ of [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc], it is the right adjoint of [sk-prop-sf-existence] for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$.

proof.text: For $Z=X,Y$, let $a_Z:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be its structure morphism. The base is affine, hence qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Finite type of $a_Z$ includes quasi-compactness by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and separatedness of $a_Z$ gives quasi-separatedness by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Applying clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] to $a_Z$ shows that $Z$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. This verifies the scheme hypothesis needed for the integral category equality in the next step.

source.place: First sentence, the qcqs hypotheses for the equality Dctf=Dbc, expanded using the cited scheme lemmas.

proof.text: Apply [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc](2) to $Z=X,Y$ and $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$. It gives equal full subcategories $\Dctf(Z,\mathcal O_E)=\Dbc(Z,\mathcal O_E)$ and equal localizing closures. Thus, writing $\mathcal C_Z=\Loc(\Dbc(Z,\mathcal O_E))$, the categories in the present statement are exactly those in the $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ instance of the general existence theorem. The equality takes place inside the same module-object derived category and preserves the ambient morphisms and coproducts; it does not identify discrete constant integral coefficients with condensed integral coefficients.

source.place: Part (2), equalities of the full subcategories and localizing closures; the equality used by sk-prop-int-brown.proof.md.

proof.text: Use the chosen compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y)$ of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], inside the separated finite-type $k$-scheme setting. By [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data], $j$ is a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ is proper, as required by the general existence theorem. The functor of [det-prop-int-brown-construction] is the restriction of $Rp_*j_!$ to $\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal C_Y$. Here $j_!$ on complexes means precisely the levelwise functor $D(j_!)$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek], since extension by zero of module objects is exact. Consequently, on the equal full subcategories from step 2, this functor is the restriction of the very same ambient composite $Rp_*D(j_!)$ at the very same compactification that occurs in [sk-prop-sf-existence]. Equality includes both the object and morphism actions. In particular we are not taking the total right derived functor of the underived composite $p_*j_!$.

source.place: First sentence, identification of the integral compactification functor with the general construction; module convention from sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek.

proof.text: Now specialize [sk-prop-sf-existence] to $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, the given finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and the given $f$. Its coefficient is admissible, its field has characteristic different from $\ell$, and its source, target and morphism satisfy exactly the separated finite-type hypotheses written in our statement. Steps 2 and 3 identify its two categories and its left adjoint with $\mathcal C_X,\mathcal C_Y$ and our $Rf_!$. Its conclusion therefore supplies an exact functor $G:\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_X$ and natural bijections $\Hom_{\mathcal C_Y}(Rf_!M,N)\simeq\Hom_{\mathcal C_X}(M,GN)$ for every $M,N$. Define $f^!=G$ with this adjunction. Exactness is part of the cited theorem, including its adjunction-induced shift structure; it is not inferred merely from the existence of a right adjoint. This is the general Brown construction at the integral coefficient stage, as required by the unit proof.

source.place: First sentence: this is the case Lambda=O_E of sk-prop-sf-existence; the general theorem packages Brown representability (Stacks 0A8F/0A8G) and exactness (Stacks 0A8D).

proof.text: Let $J:\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_X$ be any other right adjoint of this same $Rf_!$, with counit $\varepsilon^J$, and let $\varepsilon^G$ be the counit chosen in step 4. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to $F=Rf_!$. It gives a natural isomorphism $\gamma:G\xrightarrow{\sim}J$, whose component is the $J$-transpose of $\varepsilon^G_N$, and whose inverse is the $G$-transpose of $\varepsilon^J_N$. It satisfies $\varepsilon^J_N\circ Rf_!(\gamma_N)=\varepsilon^G_N$, and is the only family satisfying these equations. This proves precisely the counit-compatible uniqueness in the corrected statement. Since $G$ was chosen to be the integral instance of the general adjoint, the asserted identification with [sk-prop-sf-existence] is this choice itself; for any alternative choice it is the same unique counit-compatible isomorphism.

source.place: Last two sentences, uniqueness compatible with the counits and identification with the integral case of sk-prop-sf-existence.

proof_origin.place: The unit proof, first sentence: specialize sk-prop-sf-existence at O_E using Dctf=Dbc; expand the category/functor identifications and the counit normalization from sk-prop-int-brown-adjoint.proof.md.
